records.quote: Lemma 2.5. By considering (4) [h_F(x;phi,alpha) = alpha h(x)(phi + H(x))^{...}], we have - if r(x) is increasing and phi >= 1 then r_F(x;phi,alpha) is increasing. - if r(x) is decreasing and phi >= 1 then r_F(x;phi,alpha) is decreasing.
records.family: NLCH_G family: new lifetime distribution generated from cumulative hazard rate H(x) of baseline G; hazard h_F(x) = alpha h(x)(phi+H(x))^{phi-1} (weighted baseline hazard)
records.compared: monotonicity (IFR/DFR) preservation from baseline hazard r(x) to model hazard r_F(x)

conclusion.direction: hazard-rate monotonicity preserved: increasing r(x) => increasing r_F; decreasing r(x) => decreasing r_F

records.ambiguity: Shape-preservation lemma rather than a comparison of two random variables; included because it bounds the model hazard behavior relevant to ordering results. Parameter symbols are OCR-damaged (alpha, phi inferred from context).
